neighbours.label: the noun for a representation of how things really are, after verbs like give/offer/be ('an accurate picture of', 'a true reflection of', 'a rough sense of', 'information about'); literal pictures, mirror reflections and ideas for things stay quiet
fire: Online reviews rarely give an accurate picture of how good a restaurant really is.
Ice cores are a valuable source of information about ancient atmospheres.
These test scores may not be a true reflection of what the pupils have learned.
A single blood test cannot give a complete picture of your liver function.
The census gives a rough sense of how many families live in each district.
Official figures do not provide an accurate picture of unemployment in rural areas.
Tree rings offer a reliable record and useful information about past droughts.
Her diary gives a clearer idea of what daily life in the camp was like.
quiet: The restaurant has a framed picture of the founder hanging by the door.
Ice cores are drilled out of glaciers with long hollow metal tubes.
The pupils saw their reflection in the shop window on the way home.
She painted a picture of the harbour at sunset for her mother.
The census takers knocked on every door in each district.
He came up with an idea for a new phone app over the weekend.
Tree rings are visible when the trunk is cut straight across.
Her diary was kept in a locked drawer in the camp office.
